thread:
sam: FYI EU-west GPU pool is saturated right now, 95% GPU util for last 8m. Seeing queue depth spike and 99p tail >2s. Thinking emergency shedding for low-priority routes.
anya: ugh. which routes are we calling low-priority? can we be surgical?
derek: list I saw: 'embeddings-bulk', 'async-batch-jobs', and some internal tooling test routes. non-customer sync traffic should be first to shed.
sam: exact breakdown (short): embeddings-bulk 40% of queued tokens, async-batch-jobs 22%, internal 5%. Customer sync (chat/generate) ~33%.
lee: +1 to surgical. prefer per-route soft limits before global FIFO drop. We should avoid killing chat paths.
morgan: also consider model-fallback to smaller quantized variant for heavy tails. cheaper and reduces GPU time.
anya: can we do token-based admission control not request-based? i.e., count token budget per route. cheaper to drop a 200-token vs 2000-token job.
derek: yep. we already have token_estimate in admission metadata. can wire a quick admission rule.
ops-bot: alert: "eu-west/gpu-pool" crossing 90% util for 10m. Incident created: #INC-2026
sam: propose plan: 1) apply per-route token caps for non-critical routes (embeddings-bulk -> 50k tokens/min) 2) deploy soft-priority queueing with aging to avoid starvation 3) enable model-fallback on heavy routes 4) monitor 5m tail latency and revert as needed.
lee: lightweight config draft:
```yaml
admission_rules:
  - route: embeddings-bulk
    type: token_cap
    cap_per_min: 50000
    priority: low
  - route: async-batch-jobs
    type: token_cap
    cap_per_min: 30000
    priority: low
  - route: chat,generate
    type: reserved
    min_tokens_per_min: 40000
    priority: high
fallbacks:
  chat: model-small-qs
  embeddings-bulk: model-embed-slim
```
morgan: :thumbsup: that looks fine. add metric tags so we can measure cost delta.
anya: how do we implement soft-priority? do we use separate queues or priority-weighted FIFO?
derek: we can do weighted queues with an aging factor to bump older low-priority requests. simpler than full preemption. weight config per queue + max-age.
sam: agree. max-age 45s for low-priority during emergency window. if older, bump priority once.
lee: risk: cross-region fallbacks — if eu-west directs to eu-central fallback pool, network egress latency and cost spike. prefer local model-fallbacks first.
morgan: cost note: fallbacks to smaller models reduce GPU seconds but might increase token count if outputs less concise. track quality metrics.
anya: operational steps? who runs this?
sam: I'll push admission change to staging, lee will run canary to 10% traffic, then we flip to 100% if metrics look ok. derek takes the rollback play. morgan will watch cost/quality.
deploy-bot: rollout started for admission-rules v2026.03 -> canary (10%)
ops-bot: Metrics dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/eu-west/gpu-pool (posted)
lee: if canary shows >5% error bump for chat, rollback immediately and fall back to emergency FIFO-drop non-customer.
derek: rollback command (if needed): `curl -XPOST https://ops-api/rollbacks/admission-rules -d '{"to": "v2026.02"}'`
anya: postmortem note: capture why embeddings-bulk spiked. looks like a scheduled heavy ingest from partner X at 02:10 UTC — we should add ingestion window gating.
sam: will open follow-up ticket for partner gating + long-term: adaptively tune caps based on smoothed arrival rates.
morgan: once stable, propose we simulate burst scenarios during chaos days to validate token-cap heuristics.
sam: thanks all. starting the canary now. will update in this thread.
deploy-bot: Canary 10% live.
ops-bot: Alert cleared: util now 82% (10m). continuing to monitor.
sam: canary looks healthy at 10m. tail latency down ~30%. escalating to full rollout in 3m unless objections.
lee: no objections. :rocket:
sam: rolling to 100%
deploy-bot: Rollout complete. admission-rules v2026.03 -> prod
morgan: cost delta after 30m: -12% GPU seconds in eu-west. quality checks show small drop for embeddings bulk (cosine distance delta +0.7%). tracking.
anya: create follow-up: add partner throttles + automated post-incident tuning.
sam: done: https://issues.internal/RWD-3421
lee: nice job. saved capacity without hard drops.
derek: will draft a short runbook for emergency queue-shedding with exact commands and thresholds.
sam: perfect. closing thread once runbook PR merges. :white_check_mark:
